chunks: From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Abdullah ibn Al-Walid Al-Kindi who said:

We entered upon Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) during the time of Marwan. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Who are you?' So we said, 'We are from the people of Kufa.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no city among the cities with more people loving us than the people of Kufa, and especially this group. Allah, Exalted is His Mention, has guided you to a matter which the people were ignorant of. You loved us while the people hated us, you followed us while the people opposed us, you affirmed us while the people denied us. So Allah has made you live our life and die our death.'

So I testify regarding my father that he used to say: 'There is nothing between any one of you and seeing what pleases Allah with his eyes and rejoicing, except that his soul reaches here' — and he gestured with his hand to his throat.
And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has said in His Book: 'And certainly We sent messengers before you and made for them wives and offspring.'
So we are the offspring of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Al-Sadiq say about the people of Kufa and the meaning of death for the believers?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Sadiq (as) highlights the unique spiritual status of the Kufans, particularly a specific group, for their early acceptance of the Ahl al-Bayt amidst general societal rejection, framing their loyalty as a divine guidance. The narration links the concept of martyrdom—symbolized by the gesture to the throat—to the ultimate reward of witnessing divine pleasure, while invoking Surah Ar-Ra'd to affirm the Imams' lineage as the purified offspring of the Prophet. This hadith serves as a key text in Shia scholarship for validating the political and spiritual legitimacy of the Ahl al-Bayt against the Umayyad caliphate.
